sources.sections: The Basics; Noun + ni; Location; Attachment; Points in Time; Social Interactions and Transactions.

sources.sections: The Basics; Specifying Places; Means of an Action.
sources.inspected: Actual account of activity/event locations, contrast with existence/location ni, and tool/transport/language uses of de. Examples include a cutting tool, travel by vehicle and speaking in Japanese.
sources.qualification: Specification is a teaching metaphor, not a requirement that the chosen location be indispensable to the activity. Later quantity, cause, material-production and copular-de discussions are not imported as new exercised distinctions.

sources.sections: The Basics; Physical Destinations and Directions; Difference between ni and he; final link to noun-modifying no.
sources.inspected: Explicit particle pronunciation e; destination/direction with iku/kuru; both ni and he in the same going-to-Japan example; the source's qualifications about other predicates. The actual noun-modifier URL was discovered through this page's link.
sources.qualification: Do not infer that ni guarantees a completed arrival or he guarantees nonarrival. The article does not adopt a categorical claim that he is more polite or poetic, or that it freely replaces every ni. No unrestricted walk/run substitution rule is taught.

Checks.assessment: The unchanged noun versus changing noun-predicate ending distinction is maintained. [私の本]を separates internal modification from the phrase's outer role. 学生だ/です, 学生じゃない/ではありません, 学生だった/でした, and spoken 学生じゃないです are correctly bounded noun patterns. The positive-verb warning does not incorrectly prohibit negative verb + です.

Swapping が and を really swaps caller and called person. 窓が大きいです and 猫がいます prevent subject from being equated with agent. The 好き warning does not force an English-object analysis onto Japanese or categorically deny every other construction. Route and departure を are distinguished from ordinary direct objects.

図書館にいます versus 図書館で勉強します contrasts existence and activity locations. 学校で授業があります is explicitly an event-occurrence reading, contrasted with a physically existing library. This is not an unsupported rule that the spelling ある always selects に. Support for the event example combines the event-location function of で with the separately inspected event sense of ある; the exact original sentence is not claimed as a retrieved quotation.

Tools, transport, and language are correctly distinguished from the vehicle selected by 乗る. 学校に行きます and 学校へ行きます are valid alternatives; goal versus direction is not turned into an arrival/nonarrival guarantee or an unrestricted substitution rule. The clock-time/duration distinction, qualified omission of に after 今日/明日, and recipient pattern with 貸す are sound.

The companion reading and noun-list reading of と are separately illustrated, including the scope [兄と妹]が. Writing with a friend versus with a pen distinguishes a participating companion from an instrument. No categorical claim about all interactive uses of と is needed for these examples.

N2 is identified as the head of N1 の N2. Possession, affiliation, material, and time are presented as contextual relationships, not four unrelated mandatory translations. [学校の先生]が and この本 make the scope and attachment boundary visible. Nominalizing の is separately signposted.

から/まで mark the stated interval or route without requiring both endpoints to be spoken. 三時まで勉強します gives a continuing study period, whereas 三時までに本を返してください sets a deadline allowing earlier return. The article does not universalize this contrast to every use of まで or claim uninterrupted work throughout a normal schedule.

The object remains what is read in the を/は/も comparison. The deliberately literal topic translation is explained rather than offered as idiomatic English. では/でも demonstrate that a case particle can remain, with an explicit warning against mechanical deletion or combination. Advanced particle senses are appropriately outside scope.

decisions: Distinguish formation from open contextual selection and interpretation; a case-pattern drill is not a claim that all other discourse framings are ungrammatical.
Allow ni/he/made together only in broad destination/extent tasks; explain goal, direction and extent rather than fabricate uniqueness.
Time-point formation explicitly excludes range framing; feedback acknowledges natural kara with starting predicates instead of declaring it invalid.
Include noun-negative contractions and uncontracted polite forms, plus kana and mixed-kanji/kana spellings of complete noun-phrase answers.
Separate subject from agent, noun head from full phrase, and the object role from wa/mo information framing.
Exercise event aru versus physical presence, tool/transport/language de, and the vehicle-ni pattern under affirmative and factual-negative riding.
Protect tested time expressions and particle sounds from lexical hints; supply kana readings for clock/duration targets without supplying a missing answer.
Pronunciation blanks lie outside the quoted sentence and request phonetic hiragana; feedback retains the normal ha/he/wo particle spellings.
Use existing scissors identity hasami -> 鋏; do not create a bogus kana-only card reference.
No generalization that negative riding means refusal, that a time limit implies intention, or that ni/he guarantees arrival/nonarrival.

completed: 私は学生ではありません。
私は学生じゃありません。
私は学生ではないです。
私は学生じゃないです。
exerciseAccounting.note: All four accepted forms are valid; affirmative distractors fail. The visible polite-family instruction also allows the more polite negative identified in F03.
Ordinary plain affirmative だ/です-series formation, not free sentence completion. 兄 is the speaker's older brother; 先生 is used for another person, not self-address.
Polite past matches then; past/plain contrast is correctly bounded. Present and negative distractors do not satisfy the request.

Both accepted plain negatives and all distractor judgments are sound. Breadth of 'Contractions are allowed' versus rough ない contractions remains a task-boundary question, not an established wrong model answer.
Explicit subject-case formation excludes は/も; caller and called person are correctly distinguished. 呼びます is よびます, calling to/summoning rather than specifically telephoning.
Correct non-agent subject counterexample. 大きい is lexical and です functional; neither hint falsely describes an agent or leaks が.
Basic object-case restriction is visible; reading need not physically alter the book. が and に do not supply the requested object pattern.
A person can be the object; と changes the brother into a fellow participant in calling. Reference to an earlier example is unnecessary but the current sentence is independently explained.
All four labels identify the full phrase, excluding を. 本 and 私 alone fail the expressly complete-phrase task. Separate lexical hints do not identify grammatical head/scope for the learner.
Full subject phrase versus head/modifier is correctly tested; the teacher, not the school, comes. 来ます reading きます is correct.
Ordinary animate presence calls for に. The exclusion of event/activity and は/も makes the scope explicit; います is lexical いる, not an auxiliary occurrence.

Findings.title: The language-used context rejects valid 日本語を話します
Findings.defect: The visible task says 'I will speak in Japanese. Mark the language used, not a person addressed or words quoted. Use one basic particle.' 日本語を話します marks Japanese as the language spoken and satisfies those visible restrictions. Only で is accepted. The unshown target ID language-means and later explanation do not add a pre-answer exclusion of the language-object pattern.
Findings.impact: A learner who supplies a common, correct language + を + 話す pattern is marked wrong. This can teach false uniqueness or a false ban on を with a spoken language; the linked 話す word card explicitly teaches 日本語を話す.
Findings.minimalRemedy: Either accept を as another realization and explain language-as-object versus language-as-medium, or make this an explicit formation exercise requesting the language-as-means case pattern and excluding language-as-object framing. The latter preserves the existing narrow language-means target and mirrors legitimate restrictions elsewhere in the set. Do not automatically add を to basic-write-english: 手紙を is already printed there.

Findings.confidence: High: the alternative's grammar is directly supported, and the visible exclusions do not distinguish it from the requested meaning. This is not a request to treat every explicitly constrained drill as unrestricted.

Findings.title: Meaning-preserving typed spellings are omitted without a spelling restriction
Findings.defect: The four exercises accepting まで omit its recognized kanji spelling 迄; the two deadline exercises accepting までに omit 迄に. The modifier-identification task accepts 三時 and さんじ but not the ordinary numeral spelling 3時. None of these question-side instructions requires hiragana, the original numeral script or exact copying. Trim/NFKC does not turn 迄 into まで or 3時 into 三時.
Findings.impact: Correct construction/phrase identification can fail grading because of orthography rather than the tested grammar. Impact is limited, especially for the less usual 迄 spelling; this is not an assertion that the kanji spelling is the preferred beginner model.
Findings.minimalRemedy: Add 迄 to the four applicable accepted lists, 迄に to the two deadline lists, and 3時 to basic-train-time-modifier. Keep the current kana/kanji model buttons and do not create extra choice buttons solely for spelling variants. Alternatively, a genuinely desired exact-spelling drill would need an explicit visible restriction, but these are currently grammar/interpretation tasks.

Findings.title: The polite negative-family instruction does not exclude ではございません
Findings.defect: This task requests a polite negative nonpast noun ending from the では/じゃ family, permits contractions, and excludes only explanatory の/ん framing. 私は学生ではございません is a heightened-polite negative in that family, but ではございません is not accepted. Unlike the affirmative tasks, this instruction does not limit the task to ordinary だ/です-series endings or exclude heightened-polite variants.
Findings.impact: A valid but more formal completion can be rejected under a task that asks only for politeness and the では/じゃ family. This is a narrow grading/scope mismatch, not an error in any of the four current accepted negatives and not a demand to teach honorific language in this beginner set.
Findings.minimalRemedy: For the intended small beginner formation drill, add a pre-answer restriction such as 'Use the ordinary ありません or ないです endings, not ございません.' Alternatively accept ではございません with a short more-formal-register note. Do not mislabel でございます as requiring an honored third-person subject: it is also polite self-presentation.

The inspected では/じゃ negative construction combines these frames with a negative form of ある.

Findings.confidence: High that the composed negative is grammatical and fits the literal register/family request; the remedy is deliberately a local scope restriction rather than an unbounded expansion of accepted paraphrases.
